subject.title: fix(qqbot): guard mentionPatterns against ReDoS via compileSafeRegex

question: Should QQBot mentionPatterns fail closed by skipping unsafe nested-repetition regexes with this PR, or should the PR add operator-facing diagnostics before merge?
rationale: The security fix is well-scoped, but it changes the runtime behavior of an existing config field, so maintainer intent is needed for the compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Accept fail-closed hardening after proof
options.body: Merge once real QQBot/group-gate proof shows unsafe patterns are skipped and safe patterns still match, accepting that unsafe configured patterns no longer wake the bot.

options.title: Require operator diagnostics
options.body: Ask for a warning or diagnostic when QQBot rejects unsafe or invalid mentionPatterns so existing operators can see why a pattern stopped matching.

options.title: Pause for broader config policy
options.body: Hold this PR if maintainers want a cross-channel mentionPatterns policy before changing QQBot semantics.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed hardening after proof
recommendation.body: Merge once real QQBot/group-gate proof shows unsafe patterns are skipped and safe patterns still match, accepting that unsafe configured patterns no longer wake the bot.

likelyOwner.reason: The open decision is about safe-regex/config hardening policy more than QQBot routing internals, and steipete has the strongest history on that helper and precedent.
